PMID:41480428.setting: Kings Mill Hospital, a 650-bed district general hospital (Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust); adults presenting to the ED with suspected scaphoid fracture
PMID:41480428.standard: BSSH Scaphoid Standards: review in a specialist fracture clinic within 7 days of presentation, and a dedicated four-view scaphoid radiograph series at initial assessment (target 100% for both)

cycle1.result: Fracture clinic review within 7 days in 68.5% (170/248); four-view scaphoid series in 95.2% (236/248). Scaphoid fracture confirmed in 44 (17.7%); false-negative rate of initial radiographs 22.7% (10/44), false-positive rate 5.2% (13/248).

PMID:41480428.other_findings: Advanced imaging in 29.0% (29 CT, 43 MRI) with median times of 36.5 days (CT) and 30 days (MRI); median time to specialist exclusion of fracture 18.5 days. Clinical examination findings and hand dominance were poorly documented (dominance unrecorded in 66.9%).

PMID:38259058.setting: Nationwide Dutch Hip Fracture Audit (DHFA) registry, more than 95% of Dutch hospitals

cycle1.result: 3.2% (3065) treated nonoperatively. Nonoperative patients were older (median 86 vs 81 years), more often institutionalised (42.4% vs 17.6%) and had more dementia (37.2% vs 15.2%). 7-day mortality 37.6% and 30-day mortality 57.1% in nonoperative patients.

PMID:38259058.other_findings: Registry cohort study, not an audit against a standard. 885 nondisplaced femoral neck fractures were managed nonoperatively despite the Dutch guideline advising operative management, with lower 7-day (23.3%) and 30-day (38.7%) mortality than other fracture types.

PMID:39794605.topic: Implant choice for stable trochanteric hip fractures
PMID:39794605.setting: Six mid-to-large Dutch hospitals in the Dutch Hip Fracture Audit Indicator Taskforce
PMID:39794605.standard: Dutch hip fracture guideline advises extramedullary fixation for stable AO 31-A1 trochanteric fractures

cycle1.result: 138 (16%) treated with extramedullary fixation and 698 (84%) with intramedullary fixation. Mobility with frame/2 supports or better at discharge EMF 77% vs IMF 50%; no significant difference at 3 months (EMF 80% vs IMF 82%).

PMID:39794605.other_findings: Registry outcome comparison rather than an audit. In-hospital complication rates were similar (EMF 40% vs IMF 39%) and 3-month mortality was 16% vs 15%; the authors note low guideline adherence nationally.

PMID:31579723.setting: German Trauma Society (DGU) certified geriatric fracture centres (AltersTraumaZentrum DGU) and the AltersTraumaRegister DGU
PMID:31579723.standard: AltersTraumaZentrum DGU Criteria Catalogue (structures, trauma surgery, geriatric care, interdisciplinary cooperation, quality and risk management)
PMID:31579723.other_findings: Descriptive article on the certification process and registry; nearly 50 centres certified and more than 150 registered. Requirements include geriatric screening on admission or by day 1 after surgery, geriatrician presence at least twice weekly and weekly interdisciplinary meetings.

PMID:31414056.setting: Three public metropolitan hospitals contributing to the Australian and New Zealand Hip Fracture Registry
PMID:31414056.standard: Literature-derived benchmarks for data agreement and completeness (very high if ≥95%, high 90–94%, moderate 80–84%)

cycle1.dates: Records from 1 January 2016 to 31 December 2016; abstraction May to August 2017
cycle1.result: Overall data agreement 82.3% (7111/8639 items), moderate; overall data completeness 95.6% (8258/8639), very high. Lowest agreement for ED departure time (27.0%) and time of surgery (33.1%).

PMID:31414056.other_findings: 46.2% of disagreements were information discrepancies, 24.5% missing, 27.3% time/date/number and only 2.0% transcription. Registry completeness was lowest for discharge place of residence (74.2%) and discharge date (77.3%).

PMID:33879494.topic: Enhanced recovery length of stay in hip and knee arthroplasty
PMID:33879494.setting: North Devon District Hospital, elective hip and knee replacement pathway
PMID:33879494.standard: Local SMART aim: 90% of cases mobilising on day 0 and length of stay reduced by 1 day within 1 year, with increased throughput

cycle1.result: Mean length of stay 3.6 days for both total hip and total knee replacement; Model Hospital median length of stay 4.2 days (hips, 41st nationally) and 3.9 days (knees, 34th).

PMID:33879494.intervention: Multidisciplinary Rapid Recovery Group with parallel PDSA cycles: ropivacaine local infiltration protocol, oxycodone MR, preprinted drug charts, Taurus frames and nurse-led mobilisation, stopping routine MSU and TED stockings, and a ring-fenced elective ward.

cycle2.result: Mean length of stay fell to 2.4 days for hips and 2.0 days for knees (p<0.0001); all patients mobilised on day 0 in the most recent 3 months; predicted yearly throughput 560 vs 480.

PMID:33879494.other_findings: Trust moved from 41st to 8th (hips) and 34th to 4th (knees) nationally for length of stay; opioid use per patient fell from about 400 mg to under 300 mg morphine equivalent. Only 3.5% of first mobilisations were by a physiotherapist in the latest 3 months.

PMID:40345702.topic: Image transfer time for neurosurgical referrals
PMID:40345702.setting: Trauma and orthopaedics department, Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust, referring to Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham neurosurgery
PMID:40345702.standard: 100% of NORSe referrals should have images sent to neurosurgery within 1 hour; neurosurgery should review imaging and respond within 6 hours at least 90% of the time

cycle1.result: Mean time from referral to image transfer 18 hours; 36% (n=14) transferred within 1 hour; neurosurgery response averaged 18 hours with 38% (n=14) reviewed within 6 hours.

PMID:40345702.intervention: Image exchange portal software introduced so T&O registrars, then junior doctors, could send images directly without the PACS team; supported by departmental presentation, video demonstration, emailed instructions, QR-code posters and induction teaching.

cycle2.result: Mean time to image transfer 3.6 hours; 61% (n=96) transferred within 1 hour; neurosurgery response averaged 7 hours with 87% (n=138) reviewed within 6 hours; 45% (71) of images sent by the T&O team.

PMID:40345702.other_findings: Intermediate cycle (March to May 2024, n=64): mean transfer 9.3 hours, 28% within 1 hour, 43% reviewed within 6 hours, and only 6.2% of images sent by T&O owing to poor registrar uptake. Neither target was fully met; the abstract quotes 59% within 1 hour.

PMID:33933020.setting: National online clinical-case questionnaire of French physicians, including reference centres for complex bone and joint infection (CRIOACs)

cycle1.result: CRIOAC response rates 92%, 77% and 53% for the three questionnaires. 32–39% did not give antibiotic prophylaxis despite positive S. aureus documentation; one-stage exchange preferred (72–91%) for late PJI; rifampicin-fluoroquinolone chosen in 70–92% for S. aureus.

PMID:33933020.other_findings: Survey of declared practice rather than an audit against a standard. There was no consensus on total antibiotic duration, with 6 to 12 weeks chosen by most respondents.

PMID:41450368.setting: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust, a major trauma centre
PMID:41450368.standard: NICE fractures guidance: manipulation for dorsally displaced distal radius fractures (1.4.5); surgery within 72 hours for intra-articular and within 7 days for extra-articular fractures (1.4.3)

cycle1.result: 90% (27/30) underwent manipulation and plaster in the ED; 3 (10%) went straight to surgery, 2 (6.7%) without a documented reason.

PMID:41450368.intervention: Email to all T&O registrars about NICE guidance, dedicated teaching sessions, and an internal management pathway for distal radius fractures.

cycle2.result: Overall surgical timing compliance 11.6% (5/43): 10% (4/40) of intra-articular fractures within 72 hours (mean 8.6 days) and 33.3% (1/3) of extra-articular fractures within 7 days (mean 6.3 days).

PMID:41450368.other_findings: Cycle 2 measured a different standard (surgical timing) from cycle 1 (manipulation), so the cycles are not directly comparable. Insufficient trauma theatre capacity caused 73.7% (28/38) of delays.

PMID:42229155.topic: Occupational psychological crises among financial auditors
PMID:42229155.other_findings: Not a clinical paper: a questionnaire study of accounting auditors reporting that occupational psychological crises were positively associated with organisational future indifference and organisational trauma.
